summary: Partial credit memo not applied to multi-PO invoice distribution - vendor balance stuck
description: Issue summary: A vendor issued a credit memo for $4,500 against an earlier consolidated invoice that had been distributed across three POs. Only $2,100 of the credit applied to the invoice in AP, leaving a vendor unapplied credit and causing the vendor balance to be overstated. Impact: vendor balance incorrect; next scheduled payout attempted to net full invoice amount causing payment hold by treasury. Business impact: delayed payout to vendor and manual intervention required for month-end reconciliation.
impact: Accounts Payable ledger shows unapplied credit of $2,400; vendor statement does not reconcile. Treasury placed a manual hold on next payout to vendor until discrepancy cleared. Risk of duplicate payment or missed credit in month-end close.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Locate consolidated invoice INV-2025-1839 with distribution across PO-1145 (60%), PO-1170 (25%), PO-1201 (15%). 2) Post credit memo CM-2026-032 for $4,500 referencing INV-2025-1839. 3) Observe AP matching: credit applied only to POs PO-1145 and PO-1170 but not PO-1201. 4) Run nightly reconciliation job 'ap-matcher-v2' and check unapplied_credits table.

investigation_notes:
Observations:
- ap-matcher-v2 expected_distribution_count derived from invoice metadata and procurement PO splits. In this case invoice had 3 distributions but DB returned only 2 mapped GLs at allocation time.
- Root cause appears to be an edge-case race: PO-1201 had a recent PO attribute update (manual GL override) that was processed by procurement-indexer after the nightly ap-matcher job ran. The matcher treats missing gl_code as fatal for that distribution and creates unapplied credit row.
Hypothesis:
1) procurement-indexer update arrived after ap-matcher start window leading to temporary missing mapping.
2) ap-matcher lacks a retry or soft-fail that would requeue allocation when distribution_count mismatch occurs.
Evidence:
- Timestamp compare: procurement-indexer updated PO-1201 at 2026-03-10T01:59:58Z, ap-matcher started at 2026-03-10T02:14:02Z — however index propagation to payments-db shows last_sync=2026-03-10T02:13:57Z which is within 5s window; further log shows mapping_key=null at allocation time.
- Similar rare failures seen in historical alerts but not triaged; search returns 3 hits in last 12 months.
Next steps considered:
- Implement ap-matcher retry pass for distribution_count mismatch.
- Add defensive fallback: if GL missing, attempt vendor-level GL lookup or consult last known PO GL via auxiliary table.
- Add metrics and alert when unapplied_credit created for consolidated invoices.
- Short-term: manual reconciliation process and guidance for treasury to hold payouts for affected vendors until cleared.
resolution: Temporary workaround: Manual allocation applied on 2026-03-12 by Finance Ops (transaction REF-FIX-2026-0312). Vendor balance reconciled and treasury hold released same day. Long-term fix: engineering to land two changes: (1) payments service ap-matcher to add a requeue when distribution_count != matched_items within matching window (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/payments/pull/274), (2) add a vendor-level GL fallback lookup and metric emission. Patch target: 2026-03-19 (deploy to staging 2026-03-17). Follow-up actions: create runbook entry for manual remediation, add alert to pager for unapplied_credit spikes, and perform backfill job to sweep unapplied credits created in last 90 days. Audit trail: manual fix documented in Concur and general ledger entries GL-AP-ADJ-20260312.
